scenarios.title: Real browser restart at every lifecycle phase (persistent profile, clean exit, relaunch)
scenarios.expected: all storage bytes survive the restart; inspect() reports the phase's state; resume() completes to committed
steps: for each of: no marker, intent, profiles-verified, stores-verified, committed
launch persistent context, seed, drive the real controller to the phase
dump all localStorage, close the browser, relaunch with the same profile directory
dump again and compare; inspect(); resume()

checks.desc: every phase: the complete localStorage dump is byte-identical after the restart
every phase: inspect() after the restart equals the expected mode (legacy/recovery/recovery/recovery/durable)
every phase: resume() reaches committed; legacy bytes unchanged; preserved copy equals the original
after restart the current writers stay blocked once a marker exists

notTested: Clean browser exit only; abrupt kill is S2-10. The real App UI after restart is not run here (see report: React 19 on this host, the repository pins 18).

scenarios.title: Process crash (SIGKILL) after cutover writes, then relaunch: what survives, and is it ever inconsistent?
scenarios.expected: the pre-crash (flushed) state always survives; recent writes may be lost but never half-lost; after relaunch resume() always reaches committed
steps: profile 1: seed the legacy workspace (and, for 'resume' trials, drive to intent) and exit the browser CLEANLY so that state is flushed
profile 2 relaunch: run the real controller call (begin, or resume), wait D ms after it RETURNED, SIGKILL every process of the profile
profile 3 relaunch: dump, inspect(), then resume()
separate case: kill while advance() holds the lock inside a stage that never returns

checks.desc: every trial really killed the browser (>=1 process matched)
the flushed baseline (legacy workspace) survives every crash byte-identical
never half-written: a surviving marker always has its preserved copy (no marker-without-copy)
never ahead of its data: a surviving phase beyond intent always has the migrated profile data
after every crash the state is defined (legacy or recovery, never indeterminate), no lock is left held, and resume()/begin completes to committed
mid-stage crash: the lock was held when killed; after relaunch it is free, state is recovery, resume() reaches committed/durable

notTested: SIGKILL of the browser in a container is not an OS crash or power loss: the OS page cache survives it, so this says nothing about fsync-level durability after a kernel panic.
A renderer-only crash (page crash, browser alive) was not separately exercised.
The loss window is measured on this build/host only; it is Chromium's deferred localStorage flush, not a property of the controller, and is not a portable guarantee.

scenarios.title: OLD tab waits behind the controller's real lock, then writes after release / times out / is closed
scenarios.expected: serialization only: the old write lands after release; it is refused only by the 8 s timeout; closing the waiter drops the write
steps: new tab runs advance() with a stage gated open (holds the real lock)
old tab starts its real autosave -> pending request
variant A: release the gate before 8 s
variant B: keep holding for > 8 s
variant C: close the waiting old tab, then release

checks.desc: A: while the controller holds the lock the old write is pending (1 held, >=1 pending) and the workspace is unchanged
A: the controller's advance finishes first (profiles-verified), THEN the old write succeeds
A: afterwards the controller detects it (indeterminate/source-changed, next advance refused, divergent bytes preserved)
B: held > 8 s -> the old write fails with lock-timeout after ~8 s, workspace unchanged, controller still recovery (nothing divergent)
C: closing the waiting old tab removes its pending lock request and the queued write never happens
